findings.where: Whole page at desktop width (1440): the body column against the nav and footer
findings.fault: All the content sits in a narrow column, about 520 px wide, against the left edge. The right two-thirds of the screen is empty sand from top to bottom. The column does not follow the nav's grid, which runs from the wordmark out to the right-hand links at about 1246 px. It does not line up with the footer either, which is centred. The nav, the body and the footer each use a different alignment, so the page looks unfinished, like a draft with a missing sidebar, rather than a deliberate reading layout.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a laptop who came to check whether the ranking can be trusted. On a page whose whole job is trust, a layout that looks half-built makes the method look less carefully made.

findings.where: The 'Ranking method' section: its four body paragraphs, worst on phone (phone-01 is almost all this one block)
findings.fault: The section is four long, dense paragraphs in a row: paying for rank, pulling toward the area average, review filtering and badges, and the review-count sort. There are no subheads and nothing pulls out the key claims, so it reads as a wall of text. If you squint at the page, nothing stands out after the h1. On a phone the block runs about a screen and a half of the same grey text, and a reader can't skim to the one rule they care about, such as 'can a hostel pay' or 'what does the badge mean'.
findings.who_objects: The main visitor, a backpacker on a phone mid-trip who wants to confirm in a few seconds that the ranking is fair. They will give up skimming before they reach the badge and review-count rules.

findings.where: Intro, below the lead: the 'Scores weight toward…' sentence and the three-point numbered list
findings.fault: The three numbered points are the page's answer in brief, but they look like just another body list. Nothing sets them apart as a group: no box, rule or extra space. They sit between a summary sentence that says the same thing and the first section heading, so the intro states the method twice at the same weight. A skimming reader can't tell this is the summary to read and stop at.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who only wants the gist. They see three blocks of similar weight (the lead, a sentence and a list) instead of one clear summary to take away.

findings.where: Footer link row at phone width (390)
findings.fault: The row of links breaks after 'How we rank' and leaves a stray '·' at the end of the first line. The second line ('Report content · luc@…') then starts without one, so the separators no longer pair up.
findings.who_objects: Few would notice. To an attentive reader it looks like a layout slip at the bottom of a page that asks to be trusted for its care.
